## 0.5.6

- The GPU speech helper releases its committed memory after ten idle minutes and starts again on the next recording. Set `gpu_helper_idle_minutes` in config.json to another number of minutes, or 0 to keep it warm, then restart Dicta. Active meetings keep their speech model loaded. Helper sessions disable the CPU memory arena; diagnostics record helper commit, working set and cold-start time without dictation text.
- Crashes now leave a flushed panic record with location and thread, with private payload text redacted, and startup reports whether the previous run ended cleanly. Updates ask you to finish a live meeting or dictation and show save progress before installation. Quit and updates give in-flight dictations up to 10 seconds to finish transcription, paste and clipboard restoration, even with audio retention off; if still finishing, Dicta stays open. History and retained audio saves are flushed, while queued meeting transcription resumes at the next launch. Quit warns if a save fails. Failed meeting chunks show how many seconds were not transcribed and are retried during recovery, including gaps before later successful speech. Failed private-note saves keep their speech out of the transcript.
- Failed dictations remain listed in History when audio retention is off, with an honest no-audio notice; empty taps stay out of History. A microphone that stops keeps the captured words and reports delivery without replacing clipboard warnings; transient stream errors that recover do not raise that notice. A hung GPU helper has a shorter decode deadline and falls back to CPU while its replacement starts in the background; Graphics card only retains its fresh-helper retry and never enables CPU.
